The job now sets updated_at when it attaches a customer, as every other change to a customer's company does: a customer save, a company rename or merge, and the job storing a company of nothing but spaces as empty
- **Fixed:** The container image (the Dockerfile the Coolify and production docker compose stacks build) installs its Composer dependencies from composer.lock, the versions the release zip ships. It copied composer.json alone, so every build resolved whatever versions matched it that day: two images of one release could run different dependencies, an upstream release could change an image with no commit, and no image could be rebuilt as it was (built on October 28, 2026 it would have taken newer symfony/console, symfony/string, composer/ca-bundle and three polyfills than the lock's). The build now stops when composer.lock is out of date with composer.json, where composer install only warned and installed the old set: run composer update <package> and commit composer.lock. The container's own install at startup, when vendor/ is missing (the development stack), stops the same way, and stops when there is no composer.lock. Rebuilding an image you built before moves its dependencies to the locked versions
- **Changed:** The rest of /ltv answers money, averages and rates as JSON numbers and counts and unix times as integers, as GET /ltv/summary and the customer reads do. GET /ltv/subscriptions (p202 ltv subscriptions): amount, mrr and customer_ltv. GET /ltv/breakdown by campaign, ppc_account and landing_page (p202 ltv breakdown): total_revenue, avg_ltv, aov, repeat_rate, mrr, spend, cac and ltv_cac, and total_orders as an integer; by product: total_revenue, avg_revenue_per_customer, aov, repeat_rate, mrr, units (a number such as 1.5) and orders (an integer). GET /ltv/products (p202 ltv products), and the product PATCH /ltv/products/{id} and its delete's dry_run answer: price, or null for a product with none. GET /ltv/companies (p202 ltv companies): total_revenue and mrr, and order_count and last_activity_time as integers. GET /ltv/abm and /ltv/abm/company (p202 ltv abm): total_revenue, mrr and the avg_time_on_page, avg_scroll_depth and avg_video_pct averages, and the company view's last_activity as an integer. Each answered MySQL's text ("29.99000", "44.562500000", a count of "4", a time of "1793183200"), so a subscription's amount was a number in GET /ltv/customers/{id} and text in GET /ltv/subscriptions. A name, a sku, a reference or a product key stays a string, digits or not. docs/openapi.yaml now types every /ltv read. A client that compared these fields as strings now gets numbers. p202's tables show such an amount to the cent (9.50 where they showed 9.5) and a zero rate as 0 (it showed 0.0000), and the PHP CLI's tables 29.99 where they showed 29.99000
- **Fixed:** A database dropped and installed again under the same name (a reinstall, a wipe and a new install, a test loop) no longer reads the previous install's REST API state as its own. Idempotency records, staged changes, sync jobs and rate limits live in a directory in the server's temp dir, which was named by the database's host and name alone, so the new install took the old one's: a create sent with an Idempotency-Key the old install had answered was answered 201 with the old record and nothing was created (the agent-eval seed, run again after a reinstall, created none of its records), and the old install's staged changes were listed to the new install's users and could be applied to its database (an old staged DELETE of campaign 1 deleted the new install's campaign 1). The directory is now named by the install as well: a random install id the installer keeps in 202_deployment_secrets, which the upgrade to 1.9.79 gives an existing install (as does its first API request, when the files are deployed before the upgrade runs). A store that cannot read the id refuses (the API answers 500, or 503 while the upgrade is pending) and never falls back to the old name. The directory used before 1.9.79, and any earlier install's, are left where they are and never read; the server log names each once ("p202: the API state directory ... is not used: ..."): if it holds this install's own staged changes or sync jobs from before the upgrade, copy what it holds into the directory the log names, otherwise remove it. P202_SERVER_STATE_DIR, when it is set, now holds a directory per install as well (the next line)
- **Fixed:** One identity merge that could not be re-queued stopped multi-touch attribution for the whole install. The attribution worker takes the merges (two visitors found to be one person) first in each run, oldest first, and a merge whose re-queue failed ended the run with an error, so on every later run the same merge failed first and no other merge's conversions were credited again, and the conversion outbox, model changes and the report rollup did not run either (the cron log said "Attribution worker failed" every minute). Measured: a merged person with more visitor ids than one database statement can name (65,533) failed every run with "too many placeholders". Each merge now takes its turn: a merge that fails is recorded on its row and passed, so the merges after it and the rest of the run still run, and it is tried again on the next run, then after a minute, doubling to an hour. Only a failure the merge's own data causes ends its retries: that person is recorded as retired, with the reason, and not tried again until 202-cronjobs/attribution-worker.php --retry-now, which now makes failed and retired merges due again too. A lock wait or deadlock with a conversion being recorded, a lost connection or a missing table is retried for as long as it lasts and never retires a merge. GET /attribution/queue (p202 attribution queue) counts merges_failing and merges_retired and lists them with their last_error in merge_rows; merges_awaiting_requeue no longer counts a retired merge. The Attribution page warns when any merge is failing or retired, and the worker's summary line says how many failed or were retired. The upgrade adds four columns and an index to 202_identity_merges.
- **Fixed:** Product analytics (the events and attributes the pages record for the Tracking202 portal) are delivered one run at a time. 202-cronjobs/sync-messaging.php, which an operator may schedule for a tighter cadence than the cron job's hourly delivery, kept its runs apart by a file it made and deleted (messaging-sync.lock): a run still delivering ten minutes later had a second one started beside it, a run that died kept every run for the next ten minutes from delivering, and nothing kept it apart from the hourly delivery of the cron job (202-cronjobs/index.php). Two deliveries at once read the same waiting events, so each was sent twice and, while the portal could not be reached, spent two of its five attempts on one outage. Both now hold one lock for the whole delivery (flock() on 202-cronjobs/analytics-delivery.lock), which has no age and goes with the run's process if it dies. While one holds it the other delivers nothing: sync-messaging.php says "Analytics delivery already running", exits 0 and writes "Analytics delivery already running: another run holds …" to the server's error log, and the cron job's hourly run skips its delivery and goes on. The web server's user and the user a crontab's php line runs as must both be able to open that file, as for cron-run.lock: a run that cannot make, open or lock it delivers nothing and says why (sync-messaging.php exits 1 with "Analytics delivery failed: …"; the cron job's hourly run writes the same to the error log and goes on with its other work). So an install that made an empty cron-run.lock by hand, because its web server cannot write 202-cronjobs/, needs an empty analytics-delivery.lock there too, readable by every user. A messaging-sync.lock an earlier version left in 202-cronjobs/ is no longer read and can be deleted
- **Fixed:** A database installed again under one P202_SERVER_STATE_DIR (the Coolify stack's api_state volume, which keeps the API's state across a reset of the db_data volume) no longer reads the previous install's REST API state as its own. The directory was used as named, for whichever install was there, so the bug the line above fixes for the temp directory stayed wherever the directory was set: a create sent with an Idempotency-Key the old install had answered was answered 201 with nothing created, and the old install's staged changes were listed and could be applied. Each install now keeps its state in a directory of its own inside it, install-<hash of the install's id>, made (mode 0700) by the first request that needs it and used only when it is a real directory the server's user owns and its group and others cannot write; a process running as root does not make it in a directory another user owns. When the install's id cannot be read the API answers 500 (503 while the upgrade is pending) and never falls back to the directory itself. State an earlier version wrote at the directory's top level (idempotency/, staged_changes/, jobs/ and the rest) and another install's directory are left where they are and never read; the server log names them once ("p202: the API state in ... is not used: ..."): after an upgrade, copy this install's own staged changes or sync jobs from the top level into the directory the log names, then remove what is there. A database restored from a backup keeps its install id, and so its directory, which still holds what the API recorded after the backup: empty it before the first API request after a restore
- **New:** Account › Settings tells an admin about the traffic sources in another user's account, for owners who use neither the API nor the CLI. When GET /system/traffic-source-owners lists anything, an Admin or the Super user whose role has access_to_settings (the routes' own checks, asked of the signed-in user, who must still be switched on) sees a notice above the tiles saying how many sources are listed and how many need a user chosen. Its Review link opens a panel that lists each source as the report does: the user it is in, each user whose traffic source accounts name it with those accounts, clicks and conversions, and the user it goes back to or why you choose. Each row's Move back… opens a confirmation that names the source, the user it leaves and the user it goes to, or asks which of the users whose accounts name it; the move is POST /system/traffic-source-owners/repair's own code, sent the owner and target the panel showed, so it takes the same locks, offers no user the viewer may not act on, and refuses, in the panel the page lands on, a source that changed after the page was read. The form carries the session's token; the notice reads only whether anything is listed, and the clicks are counted when the panel is open
- **Fixed:** The answers PayKickstart's, JVZoo's and ClickBank's notification URLs (tracking202/static/paykickstart.php, jvzoo.php and cb202.php) give a notification that names no click (200 no_click) and one whose click is not a click of the account whose key verified it (404 unknown_click) were worded in the shared processor for PayKickstart: no_click named the checkout link's subid, and unknown_click named no field at all and said the key "signed" the notification, which a ClickBank notification is not (it is encrypted). JVZoo and ClickBank each answered no_click in words of their own to get around it. Each provider now says where its click comes from, and the processor words both answers from that, once: PayKickstart's custom_subid (subid=[[subid]] on the checkout link), JVZoo's caffitid on the Affiliate IPN URL (?tid=[[subid]] on the affiliate link) or the subid in cvendthru on the vendor's JVZIPN URL (?subid=[[subid]] on the buy link), and ClickBank's tracking code or extclid (tid=[[subid]] or extclid=[[subid]] on the HopLink). Every answer keeps its status and outcome but one: a ClickBank notification that names no click and carries a transactionTime that cannot be read is a 400 naming transactionTime, as PayKickstart's and JVZoo's already were, rather than a 200 no_click. A JVZoo or ClickBank no_click is logged with its type and receipt, as PayKickstart's was. A JVZoo affiliate's tid that is there and is not a click id is still answered 200 no_click showing the value, since the tid is the affiliate's to use for other trackers
- **Fixed:** p202 diff stops on a profile URL the server will not call, as p202 sync does. Against an install that computes diffs itself (sync_plan), POST /sync/plan answers such a URL with a 422 on source.url or target.url, and p202 diff took any failed plan as "no server-side diff" and compared the two profiles from your machine instead: the refusal was never shown, and your machine made the very calls the server had refused. It now exits 1 (validation) with the server's message and p202 sync's hint, which names the profile to repoint (p202 --profile <name> config set-url https://…) and P202_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_NETWORKS, the setting that admits an install on that server's own machine or network, and reads nothing from either profile. A server without the plan route, or one that refuses something else (an entity it does not know), still leaves the diff to your machine, as before
- **New:** A traffic source that traffic source accounts of more than one user name, which no move back clears (wherever it is, another user's accounts still name it, so it was listed again and Account › Settings' notice never went away), can be split. POST /system/traffic-source-owners/split (p202 system traffic-source-owners split <id>, and Split… on the Settings panel for a source marked owner_has_accounts or several_users) leaves the source in the account it is in, untouched, and gives each other user whose accounts name it a new source in their own account with its name, its live custom variables and its removed mark; that user's traffic source accounts (removed ones too) move onto their copy, a report filter of theirs set to the source is set to the copy, and those accounts' clicks are queued for the report rollup, so the clicks already recorded on them are reported under the copy after the cron job's next run. The custom variable values recorded on those clicks before the split stay recorded against the source's own variables. The split is one transaction that locks the users, the accounts that move and then the source, reads everything again and writes nothing unless it still resolves the same way, so a failure part way leaves nothing written; it is logged. It takes back the owner and the users the report showed (owner_user_id, copy_to_user_ids; the CLI and the panel always send them) and refuses a source that changed since, copies nothing for a deleted user or one with no record, and needs an Admin with access_to_settings who may act on the user the source is in and on each user who gets a copy. To have the source end up with another user, move it there first, then split it. GET /system/traffic-source-owners also says how many custom variables each source has (custom_variables)
- **Fixed:** Security. A user switched off in My Account › Users, or removed, kept every page, AJAX request and form of a browser already signed in, for as long as they kept using it: the sign-in, the remember-me cookie and the API keys refused them, but a session already signed in was never asked again, and each request kept it alive. Every signed-in request now reads whether its user may still act, in the read that already loads the user's role (no extra query): when the user is switched off, removed or no longer there, the session ends on that request as a sign-out ends it (a new session id, the remember-me cookie cleared) and the request is answered as signed out, with nothing it asked for done. Every remember-me key the user holds is revoked then, so a browser kept signed in does not sign back in when the user is switched on again (switching the user off now revokes them too, below). A user switched back on signs in again as usual. The sign-in, the remember-me cookie and the session now ask one rule: active is user_active 1 and not removed is user_deleted 0, so a value no version writes is a user who may not act (the sign-in let a user_deleted of 2 through). A read of the user that fails is the database error page, never read as signed in or as signed out. A request a page's script makes (jQuery's, or fetch()) that is not signed in, for this reason or because its session expired, is answered 401 "You are signed out. Sign in again, then reload the page.", which the page shows as a failed request; it was sent to the sign-in page, and the page drew the sign-in page where the answer belonged
- **Fixed:** Security. A remember-me cookie ("Keep me signed in") went on signing in after what should have ended it. Signing out cleared the cookie in that browser and kept the stored key it names, so a copy of the cookie (a copied or synced browser profile, a backup of one) signed in for the rest of its 14 days. Signing out now deletes that browser's key, and so does the sign-out Personal Settings makes after too many wrong current passwords. It deletes that browser's key only: the same user's other remembered browsers are sign-ins of their own and stay signed in (switching the user off ends them all). If the key cannot be deleted, the browser is still signed out, its session ended and its cookie cleared, and the sign-out ends on the database error page, which records the error; the key then stays valid until it expires or the user is switched off. Switching a user off (My Account › Users, PUT /users/{id}, p202 user update --user-active 0) kept every remember-me key of theirs, so a remembered browser that made no request while the user was off signed back in once they were switched on again. Switching off now deletes every key the user holds, in the same transaction as the switch-off: a switch-off whose keys cannot be deleted is not saved (the page says nothing about the user changed, the API answers 500). Removing a user already deleted their keys
- **Fixed:** A sync (p202 sync and re-sync, the sync jobs) writes a redirector's rules on the target as one set (PUT /rotators/{id}/rules), which the target takes whole or refuses with nothing written. It removed the target redirector's rules and then posted the source's one at a time, so a rule the target refused stopped it with the target holding only the rules before that one: on a re-sync the target's own rules were gone. Since this version refuses a rule with no criterion, a source rule stored without one, which had synced, did exactly that. The refusal names the source rule (give it a criterion; the value ALL keeps it on every visitor). A target from before 1.9.79, which has no rule set route, is written to one rule at a time as before
- **Fixed:** Security. A new password left every remember-me cookie ("Keep me signed in") of the user signing in, so a stolen cookie went on working after its owner changed the password to lock the thief out. Changing your password on Personal settings, a reset through the lost-password link, an admin setting a password on My Account › Users, and PUT /users/{id} with user_pass (p202 user update --set-password) now delete every remember-me key of the user in the same transaction as the password: each browser kept signed in, and any copy of its cookie, has to sign in with the new password. On Personal settings the browser making the change stays signed in; its own key goes with the rest, as a stolen cookie is a copy of one, and its cookie is cleared, so it asks for the new password at its next sign-in. A new password whose keys cannot be deleted is not saved: the old one still works, and Personal settings, the reset page, Account › Users and the API (500) say the change failed. A sign-in that stores the same password again under a newer hash (one an older version stored as MD5) is not a new password and keeps every remembered browser. A browser already signed in is signed out at its next request too (see below)
- **Fixed:** The first page a browser opened with only its remember-me cookie ("Keep me signed in", after the browser was closed) ran without the user's roles: the page signed the browser in after the app had read the user, so the app had read nobody. A page that asks for a permission refused it (My Account › Users sent even the Super user to the account page), and the menu left out what the user's role gives. The cookie now signs the browser in before the user is read, so that first page has the user's roles, as every page after it does. A browser holding a remember-me cookie and no session is now signed in by it on any page, not only on one that asks for a sign-in; a signed-in browser reads nothing more for carrying the cookie
- **Fixed:** Setup › Traffic Sources saved an account edit on whatever account the link's id began with: a save from ?edit_ppc_account_id=12abc (a link edited by hand or built by a script) changed account 12, one of the account's own and not the one named, and took its stored postbacks as the edited account's. The id is read exactly now; anything else is refused with "Pick the traffic source account to edit from the list." and nothing is changed
- **Fixed:** Setup › Redirector showed a rule with more than one destination and the Split test switch off with only its first destination, and saving the redirector removed the others, with nothing said, though the redirects split the rule's visitors between all of them by weight (the switch is the page's: neither redirect link reads it). The API makes such rules: a rule sent with two redirects and no splittest. The page now shows a rule with more than one destination as a split test, each destination with its weight, and saves it as one; a weight of 0, which the page does not take, has to be raised or the destination removed before the redirector can be saved there
- **Fixed:** p202 report losers and report winners (and the MCP tools report_losers and report_winners) with --aff-campaign-id dropped the error of their read of the campaign's payout, so a server error, a key or role the server refused, a campaign that does not exist or an unreachable server priced every click at a payout of 0: losers listed only the rows that never converted, leaving out every row that sells below its break-even, winners listed rows whose cost per click is past it, and both exited 0. A failed read now fails the command with that error's category, exit code and hint before any row is read, and prints nothing else (under --json stdout is empty and the error envelope is on stderr); a campaign that does not exist names p202 campaign list. An answer with no aff_campaign_payout in it (a proxy's page, a record without the field), which every reader of the payout read as 0 (p202 report breakeven and campaign optimize too), is a server error (exit 4) naming p202 campaign get <id> --json, as is an answer that is not JSON, which exited 1 with a hint to read --help. A campaign whose payout is 0 is still priced at 0, and a payout sent as a number (1.9.77 on) or as a numeric string (before) reads the same. When the rows a command prints could not be encoded as JSON (a figure the server sent too large to compute with), report breakeven, losers and winners, and the eight other commands that print rows the same way (rotator test, check, trace and criteria-values, tracker test and check, conversion simulate, and system cron's table), printed an error on stderr and nothing on stdout, and exited 0; they now fail with exit 4 and a hint, having printed nothing
- **Fixed:** Security. A new password ended the remember-me cookies but left every browser already signed in as the user signed in, so whoever had used a stolen cookie, or was signed in on a shared computer, kept that session after the owner changed or reset the password. Changing the password on Personal settings, a reset through the lost-password link, an admin setting it on My Account › Users, and PUT /users/{id} with user_pass (p202 user update --set-password) now sign out every browser signed in as the user at its next request, as a sign-out does; the browser that changed its own password on Personal settings stays signed in, and an admin who sets another user's password stays signed in too. Switching a user off, and removing one, do the same, so a browser that made no request while the user was switched off no longer goes on once they are switched on again. A sign-in that stores the same password again under a newer hash signs nobody out. Browsers signed in before the upgrade to 1.9.79 stay signed in through it. The upgrade adds a column to 202_users (user_session_generation, counted up by each of these changes); until it has run, nothing is compared and every signed-in browser goes on as before. A change whose sessions cannot be ended is not saved: the old password still works, and the page or the API (500) says the change failed
- **Fixed:** A sync (p202 sync, POST /sync/jobs) keeps a redirector rule that is switched off as switched off on the target. A rule an older install stored with no status, which the redirects skip, reached the target as an active rule and started taking that redirector's traffic there
- **Fixed:** Slack notices (the Slack incoming webhook on Account › API integrations, or user_slack_incoming_webhook through PUT /users/{id}/preferences and p202 user prefs update) are sent only to public https:// addresses, by the export webhooks' guard and sender. The page saved any webhook URL, http:// and internal hosts included, while the API asked only for https://, and each notice was posted with no address check and no time limit: a webhook aimed at this server's own network was called on every notice, a failed sign-in among them, and one whose host never answered held the request that sent it, so on a server without PHP-FPM ClickBank's test (which waits 3 seconds) failed while the page showed the key Verified. The page and the API now save the same webhook URLs, and refuse, saying why, plain http, a private, loopback, link-local, carrier-grade NAT, metadata or other non-public address, a local name such as localhost, a user name before the host and a fragment. Each notice is checked again when it is sent (every address the host resolves to), goes only to the address that passed, with no proxy and no redirects, and gives up 2 seconds after its address is resolved (the lookup itself is bounded only by the server's resolver). A notice that is refused or not taken is not retried: the server's error log names the notice and why, never the webhook's path, and the sign-in, change or ClickBank test that sent it answers as before. A webhook saved by an earlier version that is refused now gets no notices until it is saved again: save it as the https://hooks.slack.com/... URL Slack shows for the webhook. P202_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_NETWORKS in 202-config.php, the export webhooks' setting, admits a receiver on the operator's own network; link-local and metadata addresses are never admitted
- **Changed:** Personal Settings no longer has a Daily email report setting, and the install no longer calls Tracking202's hosted daily email service, which Tracking202 switched off on 29 October 2026. Saving the profile, the installer and the 1.9.6 upgrade step registered the owner's hour with it, and 202-cronjobs/daily-email.php sent it the owner's email address and the day's campaign figures when it asked; daily-email.php now answers 410 and reads nothing. The user_daily_email preference is still accepted by PUT /users/{id}/preferences and p202 user prefs update --user-daily-email, and stored, so existing scripts are not refused, but it does nothing
- **Changed:** The licence check allows a 30-day grace period when Tracking202 (my.tracking202.com) cannot be reached: the install counts as licensed only if the last answer for its ClickServer API key was valid and came within the last 30 days (for the Go CLI and connecting an AI assistant, a paid Pro licence within the last 30 days). The install keeps that answer in its database (202_licence_answers, which the upgrade to 1.9.79 adds), under the key's SHA-256 and never the key itself, so a restart or a redeploy does not lose it. The upgrade to 1.9.79 copies into it the answers the install already holds on disk from the last 30 days, and a key with no answer in the database yet, or whose answer the install cannot read from it, uses its answer on disk from the last 30 days. With no such answer (never checked, last answered invalid, answered longer ago, or an upgraded install with no answer on disk, for example after a container was replaced) the licence is not confirmed: every page of the web app that needs the licence is locked behind a page saying the licence could not be checked with Tracking202, and the Go CLI and AI connections are refused (402) with the same words; each asks you to make sure the server can reach my.tracking202.com over HTTPS and names support (support@tracking202.com or the support chat). Everything opens again once Tracking202 can be reached and confirms the licence. GET /capabilities reports shell and cli by the same rule. An answer from Tracking202 still decides at once, a refusal included
- **Fixed:** A redirector rule on the visitor's ISP or carrier sends a visitor the same way from a redirector link and from a landing page's offer link. The offer link compared the whole ISP name, so for an ISP whose name has a comma ("Comcast Cable Communications, LLC") an "is" rule never matched there and an "is not" rule always did
- **New:** You choose how clicks are filtered (Personal Settings › Click filtering; GET and PUT /users/{id}/click-filter; p202 click-filter). Each of the three checks that mark a click filtered can be switched off: a click from an address a user of the install last signed in from, a click from the built-in search engine crawler ranges, and a repeat click from one address, whose window is 1 hour, 6 hours, 24 hours (the default, as before) or 7 days. An address list of up to 500 IPv4 or IPv6 addresses or CIDR blocks marks each one always counted (a client's office that tests your links; it wins over every check) or always filtered (a click farm; it wins over the three checks), compared with the address a click arrives from, before privacy masks it. Test an address on the page, with GET /users/{id}/click-filter/test or with p202 click-filter test, to see whether a click from it would be filtered and by which rule. An account that changes nothing is filtered exactly as before, and bot detection always applies
- **New:** A filtered click says why: GET /clicks/{id} and GET /clicks answer filter_reason (sign_in_address, crawler_range, repeat_visit, filter_list with the list's filter_entry_id, or bot), as p202 click get and click list do, and GET /clicks takes filter_reason to list the clicks one rule filtered (p202 click list --filter-reason; not_recorded lists the filtered clicks that have no reason). A click filtered before 1.9.79 has no recorded reason and answers null, except a bot click, which answers bot
- **New:** An AI assistant connected through p202 mcp reads and changes the click filter (click_filter_get, click_filter_update, click_filter_test, click_filter_list_add, click_filter_list_remove) and reads the account's settings (settings_get: GET /users/{id}/preferences' answer, a secret only as whether one is stored). Tracking202's hosted MCP server does not offer them, since its connections do not reach account settings; click_get answers filter_reason on both
- **Fixed:** Syncing a Smart Redirector whose rules include one saved before 1.9.79 with no criterion (which sends every visitor) now copies that rule as "country is ALL", which sends the same visitors, instead of stopping the redirector's sync. A redirector with more rules than the target accepts in one write (200) now fails its sync saying how many rules it has, and the target keeps its rules unchanged.
- **Changed:** The hosted MCP engine prints a read answer without first building a map for every JSON value, and reads a timeseries answer's last bucket without decoding the whole answer twice, so a large answer uses far less memory and CPU per call.
- **Changed:** Building the Go CLI from source now needs Go 1.27.3, which carries Go's latest security fixes (crypto/x509, crypto/tls, net/http and others); release binaries are built with it.
- **Changed:** Customer LTV now asks for a role permission, on the pages and in the API alike. Viewing it (Analyze › Customer LTV, the customer, company, product and subscription pages, the CSV download, GET /api/v3/ltv/*) needs Access to campaign data, as the reports' money does, and so does sending revenue, events, subscriptions and next-offer impressions through the API, so existing integrations keep working; changing customers, companies and products needs Access to the Setup section; and LTV Settings (its page; in the API, webhooks and integrations read or changed, and custom fields changed) needs Access to API integrations, as Account › API Integrations does. It asked for none, so a user with the Publisher or Campaign viewer role, which holds no permissions, saw every customer's details and revenue and could change LTV Settings. An API key keeps needing its ltv:read or ltv:write scope as well


</details>
